When the height of the water level is $10$ cm, the rate (in ${cm}^{2}\sec^{- 1}$) at which the wet conical surface area of the vessel increases is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the volume of the cone& be $Vc . c .$

Given $\dfrac{dv}{dt} = 1cc / sec, h = 35cm, r = 7cm$

i.e.~$\dfrac{h}{r} = 5$

We know for a cone~$l^{2} = r^{2} + h^{2}$

Lateral surface area, $S = \pir\sqrt{r^{2} + h^{2}}$
$S = \pi\dfrac{h}{5}\sqrt{\dfrac{h2}{25} + h^{2}} = \pi\dfrac{26}{25}h^{2}$

Also~$V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pir^{2}h = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\left(\dfrac{h}{5}\right)2h = \dfrac{π}{75}h^{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{π}{25}h^{2}\dfrac{dh}{dt} ⇒ \dfrac{π}{25}h^{2}\dfrac{dh}{dt} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{25}{\pih^{2}} \ldots \left(i\right)$

Now~\dfrac{dS}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi\sqrt{26}}{25} \tttimes2h\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{26}}{h}~ ~ (from \left($i\right)$)

\left(\dfrac{dS}{dt})$h = 10 = $\dfrac{26}{5}

questions.q: Let $f: R \to R$ be defined as~$f\left(x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}- \dfrac{4}{3}x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 3x, & x > 0 \\ 3xe^{x}, & x \le 0\end{cases}$ .\right$~Then~$f$& is& increasing function in the interval
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that,& $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^{n}\right) = nx^{n - 1}$~and~$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^{x}\right) = e^{x}$

Hence,~$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(- \dfrac{4}{3}x^{3} + 2x^{2} + 3x\right) = - \dfrac{4}{3} \times 3x^{2} + 2 \times 2x + 3 = - 4x^{2} + 4x + 3$

And, using product rule, we get$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(3xe^{x}\right) = 3x\dfrac{d}{dx} \left(e^{x}\right) + $3e^{x}\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x\right) = 3xe^{x} + 3e^{x} = $3e^{x}\left($x + 1\right)$

$⇒ f^{'}\left($x\right) = \left\{$\begin{cases}- 4x^{2} + 4x + 3, & x > 0 \\ 3e^{x} ( 1 + x ) , & x ≤ 0\end{cases}$\right$

For~$x > 0, f^{'} ( x ) = - 4x^{2} + 4x + 3 = - \left(2x + 1\right) \left($2x - 3\right)$

The sign scheme of~$f^{'} \left(x\right)$~is

We know that, if~$f^{'} \left($x\right) > 0$~then for those value of~$x, $f\left($x\right)$~is increasing.

$⇒ f ( x )$ is increasing in \left(- $\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right) .$

For $x ≤ 0, f^{'} ( x ) = 3e^{x} ( 1 + x )$

As~$e^{x} > 0, \forall x \in R$

$⇒ f^{'} ( x ) > 0 \forall x \in ( - 1, 0 ) .$

So, in complete domain, $f ( x )$ is increasing in~\left(-$1, 0\right) \cup \left(- $\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2}\right) = \left(-1, \dfrac{3}{2}\right) .$

questions.q: For the function& $f\left(x\right) = 4\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(x - 1\right) - 2x^{2} + 4x + 5, x > 1$, which one of the following is NOT correct?
options: $f  \left(x\right)$ is increasing in~  \left(1, 2\right)$~ and decreasing in~  \left($2, \infty\right)$$
$f  \left(x\right) = 0$~has a root in the interval~\left(e, e + 1\right)$$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $f\left(x\right) = 4\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(x - 1\right) - 2x^{2} + 4x + 5, x > 1$

$f^{'} \left(x\right) = $\dfrac{4}{x - 1} -$4 \left($x - 1\right)$

For~$1 0$

For~$x > 2 ⇒ f^{'} \left(x\right) < 0$

Hence,~$f\left(x\right)$~has a maxima at~$x = 2$

$f \left(x\right) = - 1$~has two solution as the curve of~$f\left(x\right)$~will cut it at exactly two points.

Now,~$f\left(e\right) > 0$~and~$f\left(e + 1\right) < 0$

i.e.~$f\left(e\right) \cdot f\left(e + 1\right) < 0$

$f^{'}\left(e\right) - f^{"}\left(2\right) = \dfrac{4}{e - 1} - 4\left(e - 1\right) + 8 > 0$

$

questions.q: The position of a moving car at time $t$ is given by $f ( t ) = at^{2} + bt + c, t > 0$, where $a, b\text{and}c$~are real numbers greater than $1$.~Then the average speed of the car over the time interval  \left[{t}_{1}, {t}_{2}\right]$ is attained at the point:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: position of the& moving car at time& $t\text{is} = f\left(t\right) = at^{2} + bt + c$

So,

${v}_{avg} = \dfrac{f\left({t}_{2}\right) - f\left({t}_{1}\right)}{{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}$

$⇒ {v}_{avg} = \dfrac{a\left({t}_{2}^{2} - {t}_{1}^{2}\right) + b\left({t}_{2} - {t}_{1}\right)}{{t}_{2} - {t}_{1}}$

$⇒ {v}_{avg} = a\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) + b$

The instantaneous speed is given by:

$f^{'}\left(t\right) = 2at + b$

So, to get the point where average speed is equal to car's actual speed,

$f^{'}\left(t\right) = {v}_{avg}$

$⇒ a\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) + b = at + b$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{{t}_{1} + {t}_{2}}{2}$

questions.q: A wire of length $20m$ is to be cut into two pieces. One of the pieces is to be made into a square and the other into a regular hexagon. Then the length of the side (in meters) of the hexagon, so that the combined area of the square and the hexagon is minimum, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the wire is cut into 2 pieces of length& $y \text{ and } 20 - y$

Therefore side of square will be~$= \dfrac{y}{4}$~and hexagon will be~$= \dfrac{20 - y}{6}$

Area of square$= \left(\dfrac{y}{4}\right)2$

Area of hexagon$= 6 \times \dfrac{3}{4}\left(\dfrac{20 - y}{6}\right)2$

Total~area$= \dfrac{y2}{16} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\left(20 - y\right)2}{24}$

On differentiating,

$A^{'}\left(y\right) = \dfrac{2y}{16} + \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}\left(20 - y\right)\left(- 1\right)}{24}$

$A^{'}\left(y\right) = 0aty = \dfrac{40\sqrt{3}}{3 + 2\sqrt{3}}$

Length of side of regular hexagon$= \dfrac{1}{6}\left(20 - y\right) = \dfrac{1}{6}\left(20 - \dfrac{40\sqrt{3}}{3 + 2\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{10}{3 + 2\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: The set of all& $a \in \mathbb{R}$~for which the equation~$x | x - 1 | + | x + 2 | + a = 0$ has exactly one real root, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x | x - 1 | + | x + 2 | + a = 0$

Now taking, Case I:~$x < - 2$, we get

$- x^{2} + x - x - 2 + a = 0$

$⇒ a = x^{2} + 2$

And~$y = x^{2} + 2$~is decreasing~$\forall x \in ( - \infty , - 2 )$

Now taking Case II:~$- 2 \le x < 1$~we get,

$- x^{2} + x + x + 2 + a = 0$

$⇒ a = x^{2} - 2x - 2$

And~$y = x^{2} - 2x - 2$~

So,~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 1 \le 0 \forall x \in [ - 2, 1 )$

Hence, $y$~is decreasing~$\forall x \in [ - 2, 1 )$

Now taking Case III:~$x \ge 1$~we get,

$x^{2} - x + x + 2 + a = 0$

$⇒ a = - \left(x^{2} + 2\right)$

And~$y = - \left(x^{2} + 2\right)$~is decreasing~$\forall x \in [ 1, \infty )$

Hence, from all the cases we can say that nature of function is continuously decreasing so, it will cut~$x -$axis only one time,

$∴$~Exactly one real root~$\forall a \in R$

questions.q: A spherical iron ball of radius $10$ cm is coated with a layer of ice of uniform thickness that melts at a rate of $50cm^{3} / min .$~When the thickness of the ice is $5cm,$~then the rate at which the thickness $($in $cm / min )$& of the ice decreases, is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that the volume of a sphere of radius& $r$~is~$\dfrac{4}{3}{πr}^{3} .$

Given the radius of the spherical iron ball is~$R = 10cm$~and the thickness of the ice is~$xcm .$


Volume of ice: $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left(R + x\right)3 - \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}$

$⇒ V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left(10 + x\right)3 - \dfrac{4}{3}\pi\left(10\right)3$

Differentiating with respect to~$t,$~we get

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi\left(10 + x\right)2\dfrac{dx}{dt} - 0$

Given~$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 50cm^{3} / min$

$⇒ 50 = 4\pi\left(10 + x\right)2\dfrac{dx}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{50}{4\pi{\left(10 + x\right)}^{2}}$

$⇒ \left\dfrac{dx}{dt}\right|x = 5 = \dfrac{50}{4\pi\left(15\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{18\pi}cm / min .$

questions.q: Let $f  \left(x\right) = 2\cos^{- 1}x + 4\cot^{- 1}x - 3x^{2} - 2x + 10, x \in \left[-1, 1\right]$. If~  \left[a, b\right]$ is the range of the function, then $4a - b$ \text{ and } is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given& $f\left(x\right) = 2\cos^{- 1}x + 4\cot^{- 1}x - 3x^{2} - 2x + 10$

$f^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 2}{1 - x^{2}} - \dfrac{4}{1 + x^{2}} - 6x - 2$

$= - 2 \left[\dfrac{1}{1 - x^{2}} + \dfrac{2}{1 + x^{2}} +3x + 1\right]$

$f^{'} \left(x\right) < 0 ⇒ f \left(x\right)$~is a decreasing~function

Now~$f\left(1\right) = \pi +5$~and~$f \left(-$1\right) = $5\pi +$5$

So, range:~\left[$a, b\right] ≡ \left[\pi +$5, $5\pi +$5\right]$

$a = $\pi +$5, b = $5\pi +$5 ⇒ 4a - b = 11 - $\pi

$

questions.solution:
Given that:& A box open from top is made from a rectangular sheet dimension $a \times b$ by cutting squares each of side $x$ from each of the four corners and folding up the flaps and~the volume of the box is maximum.

dimensions of the box:

$L = a - 2x, B = b - 2x \text{ and } H = x$

$V = L \times B \times H$

$V ( x ) = ( a - 2x ) ( b - 2x ) x$

$V ( x ) = 4x^{3} - 2 ( a + b ) x^{2} + abx$

For volume to be maximum:
$V^{'} ( x ) = 12x^{2} - 4 ( a + b ) x + ab = 0$

$x = \dfrac{4 ( a + b ) - \sqrt{16a^{2} + 16b^{2} - 16ab}}{24} \left[+cannotbetakenasx < a, b\right]$,
for maximum volume,~$x = \dfrac{a + b - \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2} - ab}}{6}

$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$f\left(x\right) = x^{7} + 5x^{3} + 3x + 1$

For number of real solutions, we need to find the number of times the curve cuts~$x -$axis.

Now~$f^{'} \left(x\right) = 7x^{6} + 15x^{2} + 3 > 0$

$∴ f\left(x\right)$~is strictly increasing function

i.e. when~$x \to - \infty ,y \to - \infty$~and when $x \to \infty ,y \to \infty$

So, the curve will cut~$x -$axis only once.

$∴$~number~of real solution will be~$1

$

questions.q: The number of points, where the curve& $y = x^{5} - 20x^{3} + 50x + 2$~crosses the $x$-axis, is& _____.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let,& $f ( x ) = x^{5} - 20x^{3} + 50x + 2$

Now differentiating the function~$f \left(x\right)$~with respect to~$x$~we get,

~$f^{'} ( x ) = 5x^{4} - 60x^{2} + 50$

$⇒ f^{'} ( x ) = 5 \left(x^{4} - 12x^{2} + 10\right)$

questions.q: A water tank has the shape of a right circular cone with axis vertical and vertex downwards. Its semivertical angle is $\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{3}{4}$. Water is poured in it at a constant rate of~$6$ cubic meter per hour. The rate (in square meter per hour), at which the wet curved surface area of the tank is increasing, when the depth of water in the tank is~$4$ meters, is _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Plotting the diagram we have,

Now given,& $tan\theta = \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{r}{h}$~and let water is poured at constant rate~$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 6$~cubic meter per hour,

Now we know that volume of cone is given by~$V = \dfrac{1}{3}\pir^{2}h = \dfrac{1}{3}\pih^{3}\tan^{2}\theta = \dfrac{9\pi}{48}h^{3} = \dfrac{3\pi}{16}h^{3}$~\left\{\text{by using}tan\theta = \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{r}{h}\right\}$

Now differentiating above equation we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{3\pi}{16} \cdot 3h^{2} \cdot \dfrac{dh}{dt} = 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3\pi}\text{m/hr}$

Now, we know that curved surface area of cone is given by,

~$S = \pirl = \dfrac{15}{16}\pih^{2}$~\left\{\text{as}sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{r}{l} ⇒ l = \dfrac{5}{3}r\text{and}r = \dfrac{3}{4}h\right\}$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{dS}{dt} = \dfrac{15\pi}{16} \cdot 2h\dfrac{dh}{dt}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dS}{dt} = 5m^{2} / hr$~\left\{\text{as}\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{2}{3\pi}\text{m/hr}\right\}$

$

questions.q: If the set of all values of a, for which the equation $5 x^3-15 x-a=0$ has three distinct real roots, is the interval $(\alpha, \beta)$, then $\beta-2 \alpha$ is equal to ______
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & 5 x^3-15 x-a=0 \\ & f(x)=5 x^3-15 x \\ & f(x)=15 x^2-15=15(x-1)(x+1)\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{a} \in(-10,10)\alpha=-10, \beta=10\beta-2 \alpha=10+20=30$

questions.q: If $R$~is the least value of~$a$~such that the function $f\left(x\right) = x^{2} + ax + 1$ is increasing on $[ 1, 2 ]$~and $S$~is the greatest value of $a$~such that the function $f ( x ) = x^{2} + ax + 1$ is decreasing on $[ 1, 2 ]$, then the value of $| R - S |$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
If $f^{'} ( x ) = 2x + a \ge 0 \forall x \in [ 1, 2 ] ⇒ a \ge - 2x \forall x \in [ 1, 2 ]$

${a}_\min = R = - 2$ If

${a}_\max = S = - 4$

$| R - S | = 2$

Alternate :

If $f ( x )$ is increasing for all $x \in [ 1, 2 ]$ then

$- \dfrac{a}{2} \le 1 ⇒ a \ge - 2 ⇒ R = - 2$

If $f ( x )$ is decreasing for $x \in [ 1, 2 ] ,$~then

$- \dfrac{a}{2} \ge 2 ⇒ a \le - 4 ⇒ S = - 4$

$| R - S | = 2$

questions.q: Let the maximum and minimum values of \left(\sqrt{8 x-x^2-12}-4\right)^2+(x-7)^2, x \in \mathbf{R}$ be $\mathrm{M}$ and $\mathrm{m}$, respectively. Then $\mathrm{M}^2-\mathrm{m}^2 is equal to _________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & (x-7)^2+(y-4)^2 \\ & y=\sqrt{8 x-x^2-12} \\ & y^2=-(x-4)^2+16-12 \\ & (x-4)^2+y^2=4\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & m=9 \\ & M=41 \\ & M^2-m^2=41^2-9^2=1600\end{aligned}$
